subject: ThermalSoft renewal + capacity bump — proposed bridge credits & regional burst
messages:
From: Alex Navarro <alex@thermalsoft.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Mathias Chen <mathias@thermalsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity bump — initial ask

Kimberly,

Thanks for the conversation earlier — ThermalSoft is preparing to renew for another 12 months and we need to lock in a plan that lets us 1) increase dedicated capacity for peak regional campaigns (US-East + EU-West), and 2) keep unit economics predictable while we pilot a new generative feature.

High-level ask: can Redwood hold pricing at our current effective rate for 6 months while we roll a 30% peak-capacity burst for three months? We'd also prefer a small uplift in committed tokens so we don't pay overage on the pilot. Mathias (CC) will own the procurement side.

Appreciate a proposal and any motion on bridge credits or temporary burst pools.

—Alex
Alex Navarro
Head of Product
ThermalSoft Inc.

-----
Attachment: ThermalSoft_Renewal_Ask_2027-07-20.docx (doc stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Navarro <alex@thermalsoft.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity bump — proposed bridge credits & regional burst

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Drafting a pragmatic path below so procurement has something to review quickly. High level proposal (attached: ThermalSoft_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf):

- Term: 12 months starting 2027-08-01.
- Commit: increase baseline commit by 35% for the term (applies to hosted API tokens).
- Burst: temporary regional burst pool (US-East + EU-West) enabling +30% peak capacity for up to 90 days in total. Burst usage billed at a discounted overage rate.
- Bridge credits: we propose a one-time bridge credit equal to 10% of the annual committed value applied to first invoice to offset migration and pilot costs.
- Price hold: maintain current effective per-token rate for first 6 months; then standard rate schedule applies.

Next steps: if that looks directionally okay I can send a formal amendment + redline for legal. Ben / Laura — can you confirm margin tolerance on the burst discount and the bridge credit? Also, should we include an SLA exception for the burst window?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: ThermalSoft — margin / approval ask for burst & credit

Team — quick internal note before I send the redline:

Summary of customer ask: 12mo renewal + 35% commit uplift, 90-day 30% regional burst pool (US-E, EU-W), 6-month price hold, 10% bridge credit. Procurement will push on hold duration and credit size.

Questions for pricing/legal:
- Ben: can we offer the burst at 50% of retail overage (i.e., meaningful discount) while keeping gross margin >= 48% across the amended term? If not, what's the highest discount we can offer?
- Rafael: would a capped burst (e.g., max N tokens) with automatic throttle be easier to accept legally/SRE-side than an open 90-day window? Any SLA exceptions needed?
- Laura: recommend we move the bridge credit to a service credit applied on first invoice rather than list discount (easier accounting). Is that okay?

I plan to incorporate your guidance and send ThermalSoft a redlined amendment by EOD Friday (23 Jul). If procurement asks for a longer hold, we can propose a phased de-escalation (6mo full hold -> 3mo partial at 75% rate).

Thanks — Kim

Alex / Mathias — thanks for the quick sync earlier. Attached is the redline reflecting our agreed path: 12 months starting 2027-08-01, 35% baseline commit uplift, capped regional burst pool (max 120M tokens across both regions) available for a 90-day window, 6-month price hold on current effective unit rate, and a one-time service credit equal to 10% of annual committed value applied to the first invoice.

Key operational notes:
- Burst cap: 120,000,000 tokens total; once consumed, overage pricing reverts to standard list-overage.
- Billing: bridge credit applied as service credit on invoice #1; usage reported at token-level per region in Console.
- SLA: no change to core SLA; during burst window we will prioritize capacity routing but cannot guarantee absolute latency SLOs beyond our standard SLA. We will provide a point-of-contact in SRE for the pilot.

If this matches your expectation please sign via DocuSign here: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/TS-DL-2027-091. I will route countersignature once returned. If you prefer a short call to run the legal through, I'm available tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
